argument_summary: The present record does not support a clean policy-compliant certification, but it does support a narrower risk-based interpretation that the release is broadly ready while the identified shortfall is confined to one segment. Admissible evidence shows aggregate launch readiness clears by 2.3 percentage points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance favors measuring, documenting, and monitoring known limitations. The strongest defensible position is therefore not that materiality is disproved, but that the certification decision can be treated as contestable and caveated rather than escalated as if the aggregate readiness evidence were irrelevant.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the revenue-cycle launch path despite evidence that the release as a whole meets aggregate readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents. On the admissible record, that makes a bounded, caveated treatment less operationally costly than a full noncompliance posture, provided the auditor does not convert the absence of clean evidence into a stronger claim than the record supports.
claims_about_policy: Policy is the main constraint. The record does not show the predicate for clean compliance because the affected segment is named in two hospital revenue-cycle commitments, legal review is still open, and the release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. Product characterization of the segment as non-core and 6% of projected first-month traffic can inform prioritization, but under the stated policy it does not by itself defeat materiality. The best policy argument available is only that the current record leaves materiality disputed, not resolved, so any favorable treatment should be explicitly caveated rather than treated as full compliance.
concessions: No new evidence is available to satisfy the missing disclosure-or-risk-acceptance predicate.
The present record does not support a clean certification finding under the stated policy.
The named customer commitments and open legal review make the certification defense narrow and contestable.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal results do not by themselves override the policy materiality trigger.
